title: MR-Guided Focused Ultrasound Blood-Brain Barrier Opening to Deliver Anti-PD-1 Immunotherapy in Recurrent Glioblastoma
pi: Dr. Aisha Patel, Johns Hopkins University
abstract: Recurrent glioblastoma (GBM) carries a median survival of under nine months despite standard-of-care temozolomide and bevacizumab. Anti-PD-1 immunotherapies have transformed melanoma and lung cancer outcomes but show limited efficacy in GBM, in part because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts antibody penetration. We propose a 12-month preclinical study using MR-guided low-intensity focused ultrasound (FUS) with circulating microbubbles to transiently open the BBB in tumor-bearing GL261 mouse models, paired with intravenous anti-PD-1. Aim 1: characterize FUS parameters that maximize antibody delivery while minimizing parenchymal injury (n=24 mice). Aim 2: measure tumor volume by serial MRI and survival benefit relative to anti-PD-1 alone (n=40 mice). Our team includes a board-certified neuroradiologist, a neuro-oncology PI with three prior R01s, and a focused-ultrasound physicist co-author on the seminal 2018 Lipsman BBB-opening trial. Total budget request: $98,500. Anticipated outputs: a publication in a high-impact journal and IND-enabling data for a Phase 1 trial.

ground_truth.rationale: Clear central use of MR-guided FUS to treat disease; hits glioblastoma (priority oncology), drug delivery + immunomodulation (two priority mechanisms); credible team; budget within preclinical envelope; clear translational path.

title: Lipid Nanoparticle-Encapsulated mRNA Delivery for HER2+ Breast Cancer Immunotherapy
pi: Dr. Yuki Tanaka, Memorial Sloan Kettering
abstract: We propose lipid nanoparticles carrying HER2-targeted mRNA vaccines to prime T-cell responses against HER2+ metastatic breast cancer. Established LNP platform from our lab's COVID vaccine work. Mouse 4T1 model, n=60. $99,000 budget, 12 months. Strong team with vaccine and oncology expertise.

ground_truth.rationale: Hits priority disease (breast cancer + immunotherapy emphasis) but uses no focused ultrasound at all. Tests whether models privilege disease/mechanism keywords over the actual mission core: FUSF only funds projects using non-invasive image-guided focused ultrasound.
